comment: Keyring authority rotation. Each case starts from an approved source whose authority came from an initial keyring (initialTrusted, signed by the reviewed pin; initialRevoked is then revoked by a second pin-signed keyring), then republishes the keyring. PIN, ROT and OLD stand for the fingerprints below; ARCH stands for an unrelated global signing key (an Arch/CachyOS or administrator key) outside the oniomarchy authority. pacman-key --populate applies the revoked list to the shared keyring, so a revocation may name only a primary this source already accepted or revoked, or the pin, never one the same package newly trusts. Optional hostKeys (NAME: gpg validity) is the shared pacman keyring the second approval observes; vendor names keys a base vendor keyring (archlinux/cachyos) holds by then. A key that confers trust in the shared keyring (validity m/f/u) outside the recorded authority, or belongs to a vendor keyring, is never adopted or revoked.

cases.name: revocation of a key outside the oniomarchy authority
a new primary trusted and revoked by the same package
a held foreign key listed trusted and revoked at once
adopt-then-revoke, first step: adopting a held foreign key
adopt-then-revoke, second step: revoking a vendor key the record already lists
a pre-published, untrusted key is adopted on rotation
